Keywords: War of Saint Sabas Naval Duel
RagShortTexts: Venice and Genoa waged bitter naval war over Levantine ports, prompting Genoa's alliance with.

Variants.Content: The War of Saint Sabas began in the Levant in 1256, after the Venetians were expelled from Tyre and a dispute over Acre land once owned by the monastery of St Sabas drew Venice and Genoa into open warfare. Each republic wanted control of the Acre quarter, the trade of the Syrian coast, and the grain and slave markets of the Black Sea. Genoa turned to the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII through the Treaty of Nymphaeum of 1261, and that alliance tied the Latin war to the struggle over Constantinople. Venetian and Genoese fleets fought a series of sea battles in the eastern Mediterranean, and each defeat drove the losing side toward new alliances with the Greeks, the Mamluks, or the Mongols.

The Doge and the Genoese captains see the Aegean as a road of silk, alum, and pepper, not a sea of faith. Treaties are bought and dropped according to the profit of trade quarters and galley anchorages, and a lord who holds a harbor can sell his loyalty to the highest bidder.

Genoese crossbowmen sweep the galley decks with iron quarrels, and rowers on the benches become easy targets. Boarding parties throw grapnels and pour Greek fire through the hatches. Keep your shield up on the gangway, watch the yard for the signal to cast off, and never leave the deck unless the order comes from the master.
Wharf laborers unload bales under whatever banner flies highest. Venetian ducats or Genoese silver make little difference to the carters whose backs break hauling amphorae into stone vaults.
